“On the morning of Dec. 4, 2024, I shot Mr. Thompson in Manhattan and he died.”

nary_nodes.label: Mangione tracked Thompson
evidence: Luigi Mangione, 28, revealed for the first time that in 2024 he posed as a potential investor who managed over $50 billion in assets and emailed leadership at the insurance giant to confirm the location of the investors conference so he could track Thompson’s location.

nary_nodes.label: Luigi Mangione arrested
evidence: Mangione was arrested at a Pennsylvania McDonald’s restaurant Dec. 9, 2024, five days after the killing.

nary_nodes.label: Luigi Mangione to be sentenced
evidence: He will be sentenced at a separate hearing on Dec. 18 and the final sentence will be determined by the judge, who has full discretion.

nary_nodes.label: Double jeopardy fight expected
evidence: His federal court guilty plea is expected to kick off a double jeopardy fight in state court where he still faces murder charges and the possibility of life in prison.

nary_nodes.label: State court trial scheduled
evidence: The upcoming double jeopardy fight could stall proceedings in New York Supreme Court where he’s set to stand trial Sept. 8.

nary_nodes.label: Federal charges dismissed
evidence: A judge dismissed that charge earlier this year, along with a second charge.

nary_nodes.label: UnitedHealthcare replied to investment ruse
evidence: In his statement, Mangione mocked the healthcare industry, citing UnitedHealthcare’s reply to his investment ruse. “Unlike my previous interactions with insurers, I received an immediate response within an hour,” Mangione said.

nary_nodes.label: Mangione confesses to killing Thompson
evidence: “My travel to New York and email to UnitedHealthcare was with the intent to shoot Brian Thompson,” Mangione said in his statement.
“On the morning of Dec. 4, 2024, I shot Mr. Thompson in Manhattan and he died.”

nary_nodes.label: Mangione knew actions were illegal
evidence: The admitted gunman — who is Ivy League-educated and hails from a prominent Baltimore family — said he understood his actions “would place [Thompson] in fear of death or serious bodily injury” and that “I knew what I was doing was illegal.”

nary_nodes.label: Mangione driven by healthcare experience
evidence: Mangione also told the judge that he was driven to kill Thompson because of his experience with the healthcare system as a patient with a back injury.

nary_nodes.label: Mangione mocked healthcare industry

nary_nodes.label: Prosecutors claim no personal connection
evidence: Prosecutors have previously said that Mangione had no personal connection to UnitedHealthcare and he was never a customer.

nary_nodes.label: Thompson family calls plea step toward justice
evidence: Thompson’s family issued a rare public statement after the plea hearing, calling it “an important step toward justice for Brian and for our family.”

nary_nodes.label: Thompson family grateful for accountability
evidence: “While nothing will ease the pain of losing him, we are grateful that the federal justice system has held the person responsible for this heinous act accountable,” the statement said.

nary_nodes.label: Thompson family seeks reflective sentencing
evidence: “Now we look to the court to ensure that sentencing reflects the severity of this crime.”

nary_nodes.label: DA office prepared for state trial
evidence: “Since December 2024, the Manhattan D.A.’s Office has been tirelessly preparing to pursue a trial conviction in New York State Supreme Court for the alleged cold-blooded murder of Brian Thompson,” a spokesperson for the Manhattan District Attorney’s office said following the federal hearing.

nary_nodes.label: DA office committed to seeking justice
evidence: The Manhattan D.A.’s Office remains committed to seeking justice for Mr. Thompson and his family.”

nary_nodes.label: Agnifilo filed motion to dismiss state charges
evidence: Following the guilty plea, Mangione’s lawyer Karen Friedman Agnifilo said, “We just filed our motion in state court explaining why the state charges must be dismissed under New York’s double jeopardy protections.”

nary_nodes.label: Agnifilo explains Mangione's pain
evidence: “As Luigi explained in court today, he endured years of severe debilitating pain following a broken back while struggling to navigate our healthcare and health insurance systems,” Friedman Agnifilo said.

nary_nodes.label: Mangione believed system failed him
evidence: “He believed that the system had failed him and destroyed his life,” the attorney added.

nary_nodes.label: McDonald states no plea agreement
evidence: “While the defendant pled guilty, our office does not have a plea agreement with him,” McDonald said outside the courthouse after Mangione’s plea.

nary_nodes.label: McDonald states Mangione pled open
evidence: “Instead, he pled open, which means he pled guilty to all pending counts in the indictment. There are no accommodations or concessions, and we are free to seek the maximum penalty under the law.”

nary_nodes.label: McDonald to seek life imprisonment
evidence: “The result achieved today now allows our office to seek the maximum penalty allowed, life imprisonment, which, as I’ve conveyed to Mr. Thompson’s family, is what we intend to seek,” McDonald added.

nary_nodes.label: Attorneys argued illegal search
evidence: Mangione’s attorneys had sought to bar the notebook from being introduced as evidence at his trials, arguing authorities obtained it during an illegal search.

nary_nodes.label: Judges rejected illegal search argument
evidence: Judges in both cases rejected that argument.
